response.title: battery backup for a garage door opener when the power is out
response.answer:
To keep your garage door opener working during a power outage, you have three main options. The best choice depends on whether your opener has a built-in battery backup connection and whether you want to power anything else.

Three ways to add battery backup

Option

	

Typical cost

	

Best for




Manufacturer battery backup

	

$40–$120

	

Openers designed for a backup battery




External UPS (uninterruptible power supply)

	

$100–$300+

	

Existing openers without battery backup




Portable power station

	

$200–$600+

	

Longer outages and powering other devices

My recommendation: If your opener supports a manufacturer battery, use that. Otherwise, consider an external UPS with enough motor-starting capacity.

A garage door opener typically uses several hundred watts while running, but its motor can require considerably more power for a moment when starting. That's why a small computer UPS may not work reliably, even if its advertised wattage looks sufficient.

Example battery options

Chamberlain Garage Door Opener Battery Replacement

The Home Depot

$28.58

Replacement battery for compatible Chamberlain openers that already support battery backup.

Genie 41590R external battery backup

$99.79 listed by Genie

An add-on system for specific Genie openers, not just a replacement battery. 
BB140-BX – The Genie Company

One question to find the right backup

What brand and model is your garage door opener? For example, LiftMaster 8550, Chamberlain B4613T, or Genie 7055.

The model number is usually on a label attached to the motor housing near the garage ceiling.

With that, I can help you find a compatible backup that automatically operates your garage door when the electricity goes out, without replacing the entire opener.
